title: Aurora Health - Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
summary: 30-minute follow-up to review the Jan 18th incident, validate root cause, confirm mitigations, and agree next steps for reliability improvements. SE walked through timeline, RCA and proposed changes to autoscaling and health checks.
action_items: Jordan Lee — Share the full incident postmortem doc and annotated timeline with Aurora by 2027-01-29
Samir Gupta — Add a health-check and circuit-breaker recommendation to the runbook and PR to repo by 2027-02-02
Devon Reyes — Provide the SRE metrics dashboard access and retention requirements by 2027-01-31
Maya Patel — Schedule the controlled load test with Aurora and Redwood infra for week of 2027-02-07
next_steps: Redwood to send incident postmortem and link to S3 logs
Schedule 2-hour load test (canary mode) and define success criteria
Redwood SE to implement temporary autoscaling buffer and longer KV cache TTLs for the pilot
Customer to confirm compliance questions outstanding (KMS/HSM and audit logs)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-26 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Claire Thompson (Aurora Head of Eng), Devon Reyes (Aurora SRE), Marcus Lin (Aurora CTO), Priya Anand (Aurora Security)

Summary (auto): quick follow-up on the Jan 18 incident; align on mitigations and confirm action owners.

00:00 Jordan (AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining again, we wanted to keep this tight, 30-ish minutes, um go over the postmortem and next steps. hows everyone doing?
00:12 Claire: good thanks jordan, yeah we've had folks review the doc, a couple questions on the timeline and the autoscaling behaviour.
00:20 Samir (SE): i'll start with a quick timeline, and i'll try not to nerd out too much. so on Jan 18 at about 02:13 UTC we saw a spike in inference requests, payload size was larger than baseline, our routing policy sent traffic to the dedicated pool which at the time had lower headroom due to a maintenance pop, uh maintenance window that overlapped, that caused several hosts to hit the N+1 threshold and request queuing started.
00:45 Marcus: is that the dedicated pool you all have for us? i thought we had reserved capacity.
00:50 Jordan: yes reserved, but there was an autoscaler bug and a rolling update coinciding, so capacity was temporarily reduced.
01:05 Devon: we saw long tail latencies, the KV cache warmed slowly after the restart and there was rehydration overhead, plus some tokenization size variance from a test batch — so it compounded.
01:22 Samir: exact, so root cause is threefold, 1) autoscaler race during rolling update, 2) KV cache cold-start rehydration and 3) insufficient circuit-breaker thresholds for queued requests.
01:40 Claire: ok that tracks. in the doc you mention the "K V cash" — is that just the kv cache or did transcription change the term?
01:48 Samir: yeah that's kv cache, sorry the transcript from the recording tends to do that.
01:55 Jordan: quick q from aurora security side — priya any concerns on the retention side? we attached the audit logs but want to ensure that meets you —
02:05 Priya: looks good overall, just need clarification on SSO logs retention and KMS envelope keys rotation cadence, could you share the security appendix?
02:15 Maya: yes we'll include the SOC 2 and the security appendix link in the postmortem we send.
02:22 Jordan: great. moving on to mitigations, samir?
02:28 Samir: short term we pushed a temporary autoscaling buffer to reserved pools (+20% headroom) and adjusted queue timeouts to fail fast earlier, also increased KV cache TTL and added a lightweight warming job to rehydrate on restart. mid term we plan a fix for the autoscaler race and a circuit-breaker that drops or redirects heavy requests to lower-cost model variants when load exceeds threshold.
03:00 Devon: will increasing the KV cache TTL impact memory footprints on the nodes?
03:05 Samir: yes marginally, but within the headroom we just allocated; we monitored and it's okay for the next 7 days during the pilot.
03:15 Marcus: any regressions from the change to queue timeouts? are we seeing more 5xx or client errors?
03:22 Jordan: we've seen an uptick in 429s for a small percentage, but that prevented larger latencies. we have an alert tuning plan to monitor user-visible errors vs infra-side latency.
03:35 Claire: good, we just want to avoid user-facing degradation, if 429s spike we need rollback plan.
03:40 Samir: yes rollback is simply reverting the buffer and queue settings; we also have canary routing to route a subset of traffic to fallback models.
04:00 Jordan: ok action owners — jordan will send the postmortem, samir will add runbook PR, devon will give dashboard access, maya will schedule load test.
04:12 Devon: i can get the grafana link and retention notes by monday.
04:18 Priya: on the compliance checklist — will the logs be shipped to our S3 or do you keep them? we need retention controls.
04:26 Jordan: we can push logs to your S3 bucket or provide a secure link with 90d retention, we will include options in the email.
04:35 Claire: on the canary test, can we define success criteria — 95th p99 latencies under X, <.5% error rate, and token cost increase capped at 10%?
04:48 Samir: yes we will propose exact thresholds in the load test doc.
05:00 Marcus: what about the longer-term reliability items, like autoscaler architecture change — any estimate on ETA?
05:08 Samir: engineering estimate is 3-4 weeks to get the race fix and testing, then another 2 weeks for canary and rollout; so 5-6 weeks overall.
05:20 Claire: ok we'll align on timeline and prioritize.
05:28 Jordan: anything else on security?
05:31 Priya: please confirm KMS rotation cadence and whether envelope keys are customer-managed in Private deployments; also need to see audit log samples.
05:42 Maya: noted, we'll include that in the email packet.
05:48 Jordan: last thing — competition question, we had asked about other vendors' reliability approaches — briefly, some like mistral pitch model variant fallbacks but not the deep routing/fallback we provide.
06:05 Claire: thanks. wrap-up: can we get the postmortem and runbook PR this week?
06:12 Jordan: yes postmortem by friday (2027-01-29), runbook PR early next week.
06:20 Devon: fine. i'll prepare the dashboard access.
06:25 Marcus: schedule the load test for week of Feb 7, but we'll finalize once we see the test plan.
06:32 Jordan: perfect. thanks everyone.

(Recording ends)
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache). Customer is concerned with audit logs, KMS rotation, and user-visible 429s. Redwood pushed temporary mitigations: autoscaling buffer, KV cache TTL bump, fail-fast queueing, warming job.
